findings: Buddy has four separately traceable legs: two hind legs below the pelvis and two forelegs below the lowered shoulder/chest. All four paws contact the floor; the forward neck and head join the full moderately elongated trunk without a break. Neet has four owned grounded legs, a full narrow torso, fine lower legs, large triangular ears, projecting muzzle and a small smooth nub.

Both short torso coats are rendered as smooth bounded color planes. Buddy retains furnished muzzle, brows and hanging ear hair, restrained lower-leg detail and modest tail fringe; neither torso shows curly engraved strands or raised shag. Floor watercolor/reflection texture is distinct from coat anatomy.

The two upright salt and pepper shakers remain between the dogs; Buddy noses toward the salt while Neet gives the inadequate pair a skeptical look. Heather searches the open spice cabinet in the background. No pepper spill or later cumin reveal is inserted.

Low kitchen viewpoint, contact shadows, four-foot support and cupboard/floor perspective are coherent. Cropped provisional Heather is anatomically plausible. Finished clean contours and restrained domestic detail keep the small rescue-party gag legible.

Neet holds a canine playbow with two connected hind supports, one long supporting foreleg and one bent lifted forepaw; the lifted limb belongs to the far shoulder. Buddy holds one tentative lifted forepaw with two hind supports and one foreleg planted. Both necks and trunks are continuous, with no extra paws or detached limb roots.

Neet retains fine legs, broad pointed ears, cream bib, projecting muzzle and tiny rounded nub. Buddy retains deep chest, substantial legs, visible clearance, moderate torso elongation in three-quarter perspective and a tapering tail. The heads remain proportionate to the full bodies.
The torso surfaces are smooth color planes rather than curled or engraved fur. Buddy head/ear furnishings remain regional. Rug flecks and furniture grain are background materials, not coat texture.

The exchanged gaze and raised paws express Neet correcting Buddy before the paw-switch dialogue; TV dance silhouettes establish the Bollywood attempt without converting the dogs into upright humans. The suburban living room, contact shadows and perspective are coherent; no material finish defect found.

Neet has four connected standing limbs, distinct forepaw contacts and two hind feet below the pelvis; his full narrow torso, long fine legs, projecting muzzle, large ears and tiny nub are intact. Buddy has four traceable planted legs, a continuous full torso and neck, and real clearance under the chest.

Neet and Buddy torso contours and surfaces are smooth. Buddy ear, muzzle, brow and modest chest/tail furnishings remain localized rather than spreading into curls or raised torso shag. The patterned blanket and rugs are visibly separate materials.

Neet remains at the rain-covered window while Buddy waits by the closed door and looks back; Heather holds two unattached leashes. This matches the state before Neet joins Buddy and before the outdoor sniffing payoff. Rain and suburban garden are legible without implying they have already left.

Window/door planes, dog footing and size reduction into the background are coherent. The partial Heather hand grips the leash loops plausibly and human likeness remains provisional. The warm interior/cool rain contrast supports the affectionate closing beat; no material visual defect found.
